description_full: Open House Group Co., Ltd. operates in the real estate businesses. It provides real estate sales and purchase agency/brokerage services. The company also sells newly built detached houses; and develops condominiums. In addition, it engages in the real estate investment and finance businesses; and other businesses. The company was formerly known as Open House Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Open House Group Co., Ltd. in January 2022. The company was incorporated in 1996 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: OPEN HSE GROUP CO LTD is a mid-cap real estate business with a $4.2B market cap on $8.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 17% against a 6% cost of capital, a 10-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $163M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.29×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 19× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 6.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 36% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 11% operating margin trails the Real Estate median (23%) by 12pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.

It accounts for 2.4% of sector revenue and 1.3% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 145 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 66% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 30% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 224% and a beta of 0.98, it moves roughly with the market.
val: The stock trades 44% below its DCF fair value of $67.53, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 3%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $42.43 to $105 (P10-P90).
Multiples send mixed signals against Real Estate peers: cheaper on P/E 7.6 vs 23.6 and EV/EBITDA 2.6 vs 16.3, richer on P/FCF 25.4 vs 17.8 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.9% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 1.9% annual cash-flow growth, 7pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 17% clears the cost of capital of 6.4% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.21).
It runs a 19% gross margin and converts 2% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is a concern: cash conversion of only 0.29x.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.6x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.0x net debt to EBITDA ($2.7B of cash against $4.5B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 18.9x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.0, in the safe zone).

growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.2% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 16% of profits supports about 2.7% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
own: Insiders own 35.8%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 32%.
It returns 6.7% a year to shareholders (3.8% in buybacks).
people: With about 6,620 employees, each generates about $1.3M of revenue, 0.6x the Real Estate median.
That works out to $25K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $613K (0x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
